speaker: Doctor
text: Given your symptoms of progressive fatigue, increased thirst, and frequent urination, I suspect a metabolic issue rather than a simple infection. REQUEST TEST: Fasting Blood Glucose

speaker: Doctor
text: Normal fasting glucose makes diabetes less likely, so I need to rule out other causes like anemia or thyroid issues. Do you have any other symptoms, such as pale skin, shortness of breath, or changes in your appetite or weight? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your blood count is normal, I need to check your thyroid function, as hypothyroidism can cause fatigue and other metabolic changes. Do you feel colder than usual, have you gained weight recently, or noticed any hair loss or dry skin? REQUEST TEST: Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH)

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal glucose, blood count, and thyroid levels, I need to investigate other potential causes for your fatigue and frequent urination, such as an electrolyte imbalance or kidney function issues. Do you experience any pain or burning when you urinate, or have you noticed any swelling in your legs or face? REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your metabolic panel is normal, ruling out kidney issues and electrolyte imbalances, I need to explore other causes for your fatigue and nocturia, such as sleep apnea or medication side effects. Do you snore loudly or wake up feeling unrefreshed, and are you currently taking any medications that might affect urination? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the urinalysis is normal, we can rule out infection or significant kidney disease. Do you have any history of heart problems, or do you experience shortness of breath when lying flat or walking up stairs? REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal echocardiogram, heart failure is unlikely, so I need to consider sleep disorders or neurological issues given your persistent fatigue and nocturia. Do you have a history of loud snoring or witnessed apneas, and do you experience any numbness, tingling, or muscle weakness in your limbs? REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography

speaker: Doctor
text: All major systemic, metabolic, cardiac, and sleep-related causes for your fatigue and nocturia have been ruled out by normal test results. Given the absence of organic pathology, I suspect a functional or psychological etiology such as chronic fatigue syndrome or depression. DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
